Verification console fixtures

These files retain the complete stdout and completed JSON from the unchanged
Python verification producer. They are independent expected bytes, not output
generated by the Rust report renderer. Capture date: 2026-10-18.

Producer
  scripts/verify_collation_locales.py
  SHA256 083c685a2a15cd5db564049267eb521434eb50396adadee9c13d5899ddfdb026
Interpreter
  CPython 3.12.14, built-in Unicode 15.0.0 data
  Executable SHA256 fa67443527ed9647f760d807e2a38f26340757123e643c4639cf273ed15d5ea7
Observer
  crates/locale-tools/tests/support/collation-words-fixture.rs
  Source SHA256 9da8014b19b1e506cc91e468d9b4ffb4d0da6bef51c49946c2bb5c682907193f
  Executable SHA256 16940545341e0116935806faca020ee81e84ca141487561783cd572392fced70

The producer selected variant 0 and only en_US, using candidates.json as its
literal candidate input. The observer recorded all 62 role calls, including
the 29 complete block inputs for each role. Candidate/reference inputs matched.
All block comparisons succeeded with identity output, so all 29 baseline sets
were empty. Alphabet and digit comparisons retained errors. The verifier exited
0 and wrote a complete report with 0 of 1 locales verified.

The four .stderr files are the literal raw replies. Alphabet statuses were
candidate 77 and reference 0. Digit statuses were candidate 0 and reference 23.
The unchanged producer decoded both roles' stderr with UTF-8 replacement when
either status failed. Each raw reply matched the observer's retained stream.
The malformed sequences deliberately include overlong forms, an encoded
surrogate and a truncated sequence. Successful-peer stderr is retained too.

errors.stdout preserves both the locale line and final summary, including LF.
errors.json preserves the complete report's bytes, key order and formatting.
The samples cover all quote choices, backslashes, ASCII controls/DEL, printable
letters/marks/symbols, and Unicode-15 separator/control/format/private/unassigned
characters, including a supplementary nonprintable value. No normalization or
conversion of these fixture bytes is permitted.

The rendering contract is CPython v3.12.14 unicode_repr and its generated
Unicode-15 printability classification:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Objects/unicodeobject.c
  https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Tools/unicode/makeunicodedata.py

The Rust test supplies these observed error strings and the empty block sets.
It compares complete console and JSON bytes. It does not invoke Python or a
native collator. This is an observed formatting/bookkeeping fixture, not native
collation correctness, measurement-build parity or a general Python repr suite.
